news.title: CISA adds two actively exploited flaws to must-patch list — Adobe Commerce and Google Brotli
news.excerpt: CISA added two actively exploited vulnerabilities (Adobe Commerce CVE-2026-XXXXX, Google Brotli CVE-2026-YYYYY) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. If you run Adobe Commerce/Magento or use Google Brotli, patch immediately at about.adobe.com and github.com/google/brotli.

news.title: CISA warns: GitLab and Cisco flaws under active attack — update now at vendor sites
news.excerpt: CISA added two actively exploited vulnerabilities (GitLab CVE-2026-97229, Cisco CVE-2026-76418) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct 29. If you run GitLab or Cisco firewalls, apply vendor patches immediately at about.gitlab.com/releases/ and cisco.com/security.

news.title: CISA adds three new actively exploited vulnerabilities to must-patch list — Adobe Commerce, Google Brotli, Collabora Online
news.excerpt: CISA added three new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-48356 affects Adobe Commerce and Magento (unrestricted file upload). CVE-2026-111497 affects Google Brotli (used in Chrome and many apps). CVE-2026-110447 affects Collabora Online (OS command injection). Patch Adobe Commerce/Magento, update Chrome and any software using Brotli, and update Collabora Online immediately. Source: CISA.gov October 27 and 23 2026

news.title: Chrome's 7th Zero-Day This Year Is Actively Exploited — Update Now
news.excerpt:
Google just patched Chrome's seventh actively exploited zero-day of 2026.
That's seven times this year that attackers found a hole in Chrome
before Google did — and used it against real people.

The flaw (vulnerability) lives in Chrome's V8 JavaScript engine.
Visit a malicious website and the code runs on your computer — no
clicks, no downloads, just loading the page. Google confirmed active
exploitation. CISA added it to their "must-patch-now" list.

What to do: Open Chrome. Click the three…

news.title: CISA alert: Adobe Commerce and Google Brotli flaws actively exploited — patch immediately
news.excerpt: Update Adobe Commerce/Magento and your browser to latest versions — check cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog for details

news.title: CISA flags exploited Windows zero-day — patch at Settings > Windows Update by October 16
news.excerpt: CISA added CVE-2026-96207, an actively exploited Windows Shell zero-day, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 13. Microsoft fixed it in the October Patch Tuesday release (1,413 total vulnerabilities addressed). Federal agencies must apply the patch by October 16; you should update promptly. Open Settings > Windows Update and check for updates now.

posts.title: AI voice clones can sound like your family — use a safe word and call back on a saved number
posts.summary: Hang up and call back on a number you already have saved. Agree on a family safe word now — ask for it on any emergency money call. A cloned voice cannot answer a phone you dial yourself. Source: FBI IC3, FTC Consumer Alerts, SafeBrowz 2026 guide.
posts.truth: I've had customers walk in shaking after getting a call that sounded exactly like their grandkid in trouble. The voice was perfect. The panic was real. The only thing that stopped them was calling the real number.

posts.title: Windows 11 has free built-in backup — File History and OneDrive protect your files automatically
posts.summary: Turn on File History at Settings > System > Storage > Advanced storage settings > Backup options (plug in an external drive first). Turn on OneDrive folder backup at OneDrive settings > Sync and backup > Manage backup — both free and built into Windows. Microsoft just fixed a File History bug in the October 2026 update.
posts.truth: I see people lose everything — photos, taxes, business records — because "I meant to back up." The built-in tools do it while you sleep. No subscription. No extra software.

posts.title: Fiber internet expanding in Lake City — Clearwave Fiber now at 20% availability, check your address
posts.summary: BroadbandNow data (Oct 31, 2026) shows Clearwave Fiber at 20.3% availability in Lake City with speeds up to 7 Gbps. AT&T Fiber reaches 80%, Xfinity cable/fiber at 68.8%. Check your exact address at broadbandnow.com/Florida/Lake-City or clearwavefiber.com.
posts.truth: Most Lake City folks don't realize fiber has quietly reached their neighborhood. I check addresses for customers all the time — they're usually surprised.

posts.title: Firefox 159 adds Smart Window price-watch and sidebar passwords — free update at firefox.com
posts.summary: Firefox 159 (released Oct 27) adds Smart Window to watch pages for price drops or restocks, puts saved passwords in the sidebar by default, and uses native macOS sharing. Update free at firefox.com or click Menu → Help → About Firefox.
posts.truth: I've been using Firefox since version 2. It's the only browser that respects your privacy by default — no tracking, no data harvesting, just a browser that works for you.

posts.title: Best free password manager 2026 — Bitwarden unlimited devices open source or Proton Pass with email aliases and built-in 2FA
posts.summary: Bitwarden offers unlimited passwords and devices for free with open-source code at bitwarden.com. Proton Pass adds email aliases and built-in two-factor authentication free at proton.me/pass. Both work on Windows, Mac, Linux, phones. Source: Security.org, TechDeft, ITsFOSS 2026 comparisons
posts.truth: People reuse the same three passwords everywhere because they can't remember more. A password manager fixes this completely. Bitwarden's free tier is genuinely unlimited — no device limit, no password limit. Proton Pass is the choice if you want email aliases (hide your real email when signing up) and 2FA built in without a separate app.

posts.title: Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2 are the new supported versions — free upgrade at Settings > Windows Update if you are on 24H2 Home or Pro
posts.summary: Windows 11 24H2 Home and Pro reached end of updates October 13 2026. Microsoft now supports 25H2 and 26H2 with monthly security patches. The upgrade is free — go to Settings > Windows Update and check for updates. If your PC says it's up to date on 24H2 you need to manually trigger the version upgrade. Source: Microsoft Support KB5127648 October 13 2026
posts.truth: I've had customers bring in PCs that "work fine" but haven't had a security patch in months. Windows won't always offer the version upgrade automatically — you have to click "Check for updates" and sometimes toggle "Get the latest updates as soon as they're available" in Advanced options.

posts.title: Windows 11 Live Captions transcribes any audio free — great for videos without subtitles
posts.summary: Windows 11 has a free built-in Live Captions feature that transcribes any audio playing on your PC in real time. Press Win+Ctrl+L to turn it on. It works offline for English and works on any video, podcast, or meeting. No upload, no account, no cost. Free at microsoft.com/windows/tips/live-captions or just press Win+Ctrl+L.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize this feature exists — it's been in Windows 11 since 2022 and keeps getting better. I show it to customers who struggle to hear videos or watch content in noisy environments, and they're always surprised it's free and offline.

posts.title: Windows can stop ransomware from encrypting your files free — Controlled Folder Access is built in
posts.summary: Windows 11 has a free ransomware shield called Controlled Folder Access. It blocks unauthorized apps from encrypting your Documents, Pictures, and other folders. Turn it on: Settings → Privacy & security → Windows Security → Virus & threat protection → Manage ransomware protection → On.
posts.truth: I turn this on for every customer. It's free, built in, and stops the one thing that makes people cry — losing their photos and documents to ransomware.

posts.title: Windows has free built-in troubleshooters for internet audio printer and updates — no download needed
posts.summary: Windows 11 includes free troubleshooters for internet connections, audio problems, printer issues, Windows Update, and more. Find them at Settings → System → Troubleshoot → Other troubleshooters. Click "Run" next to any problem area.
posts.truth: I watch customers spend hours Googling fixes for things Windows can diagnose itself. The built-in troubleshooters aren't magic, but they solve about half the calls I get — for free.

posts.title: One click in Windows Security turns on free ransomware protection — Controlled Folder Access blocks unauthorized encryption
posts.summary: Windows 11 has a free ransomware shield built in called Controlled Folder Access. It stops unknown apps from encrypting your documents, pictures, and desktop folders. Open Windows Security (type "Windows Security" in Start), click Virus & threat protection, then Manage ransomware protection, and turn on Controlled Folder Access. Takes 30 seconds. Source: Microsoft Support, How-To Geek, Pureinfotech
posts.truth: Ransomware doesn't care if you're a "small target." It's automated — it hits everyone. Controlled Folder Access is the one setting that actually stops the encryption from happening. It's free, already installed, and I turn it on for every single customer. Most people have never heard of it.
